text:
alex: Heads-up — scheduling a maintenance window for az-east1 this Thu 02:00–03:30 UTC. Goal: NIC microcode push + rolling GPU node reboots. Expect ~10% capacity reduction in az-east1 during the window.
priya: How many nodes per cohort? impact on Dedicated pools?
alex: Cohorts of 12 nodes, 6m cadence per cohort. Dedicated pools will be excluded where possible but a small subset (non-SLA low-priority) may be touched for thermal PDU checks.
cj: Can we route traffic to eu-west1 for inference-heavy jobs? Any cross-region egress cost estimate?
alex: Yes; smart-routing policy will shift best-effort requests to eu-west1/us-central. Egress hit is modest for control plane only, cores keep local weights. Rough cost: ~$120/hr additional egress if we see sustained 20% failover — we won’t see that peak.
marta: What about KV cache warmup after nodes rejoin? Last time we saw a latency spike for 15–20m.
alex: Good call. Plan includes KV-seed step: after each cohort rejoin we'll run background priming from our cache-warm job (script below). That should cut cold-start tail.
priya: paste the script?
alex: ```bash
# run from ops-host
for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l app=kv-warm -o name); do
  kubectl exec $pod -- /opt/kv_warm --keys 10000 --concurrency 4
done
```
cj: Nice. Any fallback if NIC push flakes? Rollback plan?
alex: If NIC microcode fails sanity checks (packet drops >0.05% or NIC errors on kern_logs), we abort remaining cohorts and rollback to previous microcode via bmc-flash. We also have a pre-seeded standby pool to take overflow.
infra-bot: Maintenance ticket INFRA-2026 created: https://tracker/redwood/INFRA-2026 — window Thu 02:00 UTC.
marta: Oncall overlap? I'm oncall Thu 00:00–08:00 UTC so I'll handle immediate ops.
priya: Any customer comms prepared for Dedicated customers?
alex: Draft is in the ticket. Key points: minimal impact, cross-region routing, can opt-out for dedicated pools (we will coordinate). Send me the customer list and I'll mark exclusions.
cj: Suggest adding a quick smoke test post-cohort: `model-serve healthcheck --warmup && tracer run --latency 95`
alex: Agree. We'll gate cohort proceed on healthcheck success. If latency 95th > 350ms for >2 consecutive checks, we pause and investigate.
marta: Are there capacity-backing nodes available if a cohort hangs?
alex: Yes — we have a small hot spare pool (20 nodes) reserved for this window. We'll trigger auto-backfill from spot quotas if needed.
priya: One more ask — add a post-mortem checklist: check NTP drift, BMC flaps, nvme SMART. Last time nvme contributed to longer rejoin.
alex: Added to the ticket checklist.
infra-bot: Reminder scheduled 2 hours before window.
priya: Thanks. I'll update runbook with the CLI snippets and customer exclusion list. :thumbsup:
alex: Thanks all — will post final start message 30m before the window and ping @marta on any anomalies.
